summary: This note covers the song "Some Enchanted Evening" and its performers in stage productions of the show. In the original Broadway production, former Metropolitan Opera bass Ezio Pinza sang it and won the 1950 Tony Award for Best Actor, making him popular with audiences who normally avoided opera. The note also mentions later revivals: Philip Quast won an Olivier Award in the 2001 London revival, and Paulo Szot won a Tony in the 2008 New York revival.
one_line: Wiki note on the song "Some Enchanted Evening" and the actors who sang it in Broadway and revival productions.
key_facts: In the original Broadway production, "Some Enchanted Evening" was sung by former Metropolitan Opera bass Ezio Pinza.
Ezio Pinza won the Tony Award for Best Actor in 1950 for his role in the show.
The song made Ezio Pinza a favorite with audiences and listeners who normally did not attend or listen to opera.
In the 2001 London revival of the show, Philip Quast won an Olivier Award for Best Actor.
Philip Quast won the Olivier Award for his role as Emile in the 2001 London revival.
Seven years after the 2001 London revival, international opera singer Paulo Szot won a Tony for his portrayal in the 2008 New York revival.
Paulo Szot is described as an international opera singer.
The 2008 New York revival is the production in which Paulo Szot won a Tony.
